values.TIP – Cylinder head bolt: Tighten all the cylinder head tightening bolts evenly in the tightening order to 32 N·m (3.2 kgf·m, 24 lb·ft). Remove the one bolt according to the tightening order. When doing so, do not remove the other bolts. Retighten the bolt to 16 N·m (1.6 kgf·m, 12 lb·ft), and then tighten it further to reach the specified angle (60°). Remove the remaining bolts one by one in the same manner and retighten them. Finally, tighten all the bolts to reach the specified angle (60°). Total tightening angle: 60° + 60° = 120° (The first and second time, be sure to apply molybdenum disulfide grease to the bolt threads and seats as well as to both sides of the lock washers.)
values.TIP – Breather plate bolt: When installing the breather plate, apply locking agent (LOCTITE®) to the threaded holes (female threads) of the cylinder head cover.
values.TIP – Primary drive gear nut: 1. Thoroughly clean the threaded portion of the crankshaft, contact surface of the washer, and threaded portion and contact surface of the primary drive gear nut to remove the oil. 2. Apply molybdenum disulfide grease to the threaded portion of the crankshaft, the contact surface of the washer, and contact surface and threaded portion of the primary drive gear nut. 3. Tighten the primary drive gear nut 170 N·m (17 kgf·m, 125 lb·ft).

values.Gearing guidance: Lower the secondary ratio (fewer rear teeth) for courses with long straights, raise it for courses with many corners; set so max revs come near the end of the longest straight without over-revving; prioritise the section with most effect on lap time.
values.After fitting a softer fork spring: Rebound: turn out 1–2 clicks; compression: turn in 1–2 clicks
values.After fitting a stiffer fork spring: Rebound: turn in 1–2 clicks; compression: turn out 1–2 clicks
values.After fitting a softer shock spring: Run rebound 1–2 clicks out (less rebound), then fine-tune; reset sunken length 90–100 mm
values.After fitting a stiffer shock spring: Run rebound 1–2 clicks in (more rebound), then fine-tune; reset sunken length 90–100 mm
values.Rider-weight table: Not printed — the manual gives spring options by rate (SOFT to STIFF) and a sunken-length target, not a rider-weight chart.
values.Symptom chart increments: Shock: rebound 2-click steps, low-speed compression 1-click steps, high-speed compression 1/6-turn steps; fork: about 2 clicks, oil 5–10 cm³ steps; sunken length 95–100 mm for low-front / 90–95 mm for high-front posture

records.notes: The manual does not key springs to rider weight; options are listed by rate with part numbers and I.D. marks, set via sunken length. Spring tables read from the PDF table cells of the same publication and checked against the text extract.

records.statement: Yamaha's 2021 YZ250X owner's service manual lists optional fork springs from 3.9 N/mm to 4.7 N/mm (STD 4.3 N/mm) and shock springs from 42 N/mm to 56 N/mm (STD 48 N/mm), with 90–100 mm rider sunken length and 2 drive / 6 rear sprocket options.

values.Gearing guidance: Lower the secondary ratio (fewer rear teeth) for courses with long straights, raise it for courses with many corners; set so max revs come near the end of the longest straight without over-revving; prioritise the section with most effect on lap time.
values.After fitting a softer fork spring: Rebound: turn out 1–2 clicks; compression: turn in 1–2 clicks
values.After fitting a stiffer fork spring: Rebound: turn in 1–2 clicks; compression: turn out 1–2 clicks
values.After fitting a softer shock spring: Run rebound 1–2 clicks out (less rebound), then fine-tune; reset sunken length 90–100 mm
values.After fitting a stiffer shock spring: Run rebound 1–2 clicks in (more rebound), then fine-tune; reset sunken length 90–100 mm
values.Rider-weight table: Not printed — the manual gives spring options by rate (SOFT to STIFF) and a sunken-length target, not a rider-weight chart.
values.Symptom chart increments: Shock: rebound 2-click steps, low-speed compression 1-click steps, high-speed compression 1/6-turn steps; fork: about 2 clicks, oil 5–10 cm³ steps; sunken length 95–100 mm for low-front / 90–95 mm for high-front posture
values.Unequal-pitch note: Unequal-pitch spring is softer initially than the equal-pitch spring and harder to bottom; spec varies by color and quantity of I.D. marks

records.notes: The manual does not key springs to rider weight; options are listed by rate with part numbers and I.D. marks, set via sunken length. values.Gearing guidance: Lower the secondary ratio (fewer rear teeth) for courses with long straights, raise it for courses with many corners; set so max revs come near the end of the longest straight without over-revving; prioritise the section with most effect on lap time.
values.After fitting a softer fork spring: Rebound: turn out 1–2 clicks; compression: turn in 1–2 clicks
values.After fitting a stiffer fork spring: Rebound: turn in 1–2 clicks; compression: turn out 1–2 clicks
values.After fitting a softer shock spring: Run rebound 1–2 clicks out (less rebound), then fine-tune; reset sunken length 90–100 mm
values.After fitting a stiffer shock spring: Run rebound 1–2 clicks in (more rebound), then fine-tune; reset sunken length 90–100 mm
values.Rider-weight table: Not printed — the manual gives spring options by rate (SOFT to STIFF) and a sunken-length target, not a rider-weight chart.
values.Symptom chart increments: Shock: rebound 2-click steps, low-speed compression 1-click steps, high-speed compression 1/6-turn steps; fork: about 2 clicks, oil 5–10 cm³ steps; sunken length 95–100 mm for low-front / 90–95 mm for high-front posture
values.Unequal-pitch note: Unequal-pitch spring is softer initially than the equal-pitch spring and harder to bottom; spec varies by color and quantity of I.D. marks

records.notes: The manual does not key springs to rider weight; options are listed by rate with part numbers and I.D. marks, set via sunken length. Spring tables read from the PDF table cells of the same publication and checked against the text extract.
